title: This Man Ate an Entire Airplane, Piece by Piece
description:
The man who ate an airplane: Michel Lotito, a French entertainer known as Monsieur Mangetout ("Mr. Eats-All"), cut up a Cessna 150 and swallowed it between 1978 and 1980.

He sawed the metal into bite-size pieces and swallowed them like pills with mineral oil and lots of water. Guinness World Records gave him a brass plaque for the world's strangest diet, and he ate that too. Over his life he also claimed bicycles, shopping carts, TV sets and a coffin. His own doctor told Guinness they never found a valid medical explanation. Snopes points out that nobody ever documented the whole plane bite by bite.

Please don't try this: swallowing metal or glass can be deadly.

Sources:
- Guinness World Records, "The man who ate metal: Monsieur Mangetout's strange diet" (2022): https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/news/2022/10/the-man-who-ate-metal-monsieur-mangetouts-strange-diet-722640
- Snopes, "Meet Michel Lotito, the Man Who Ate an Entire Airplane... or So He Claimed" (2022): https://www.snopes.com/news/2022/03/07/michel-lotito-ate-entire-airplane/
- Wikipedia, Michel Lotito: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michel_Lotito

human_angle: Every viral retelling sells the airplane as proven; we keep the honest version: Guinness credited him and even watched him eat its own plaque, but nobody ever documented the whole plane bite by bite, so the video ends on that doubt instead of on the myth.

questions.a: Michel Lotito, a French entertainer nicknamed Monsieur Mangetout. Guinness World Records says he ate a Cessna 150 between 1978 and 1980, about two years in total.

questions.q: How did Michel Lotito eat a plane?
questions.a: He cut the metal into small bite-size pieces and swallowed them like pills, with mineral oil and large amounts of water, according to Guinness World Records.

questions.q: Is it true that a man ate a whole airplane?
questions.a: Guinness World Records reports it and gave him a record for the world's strangest diet, but Snopes notes that the full airplane was never independently documented.

demand.evidence: Guinness World Records feature (Oct 2022) and Snopes fact-check (Mar 2022) both target this search; still recirculating in 2024-2025 (UNILAD Tech Feb 2024, BioBioChile Sep 2025, CNN Chile)
